messages.body_plain:
Hi Vincent,
Thanks for the update. We actually have Phillips Actiwatch and Geneactiv devices. I tested the sleep diaries with the Phillips Actiwatches and received the same error as the Geneactiv devices. I am able to run the Geneactiv converted to counts data without sleep diaries without an error as well as the Phillips Actiwatch data without sleep diaries but as soon as I include the sleep diaries I am running into the error described above. I am using GGIR version 3.1-2.

Thank you,
Aaron

Hi Vincent,
I added these two lines in g.part3 and g.part4 after the extract_params function and the assignment of params_sleep to params:

params$params_sleep$HASPT.algo = "notused"

params_sleep$HASPT.algo = "notused"

I noticed that in both parts they would default to "HDCZA" despite passing "notused" initially in the main code. I couldn't find why it was defaulting to HDCZA but this is a bandaid solution. Using this I have successfully processed both the GeneActiv (counts converted) and Phillips Actiwatch (counts) data with sleep diaries without errors and it looks like the sleep diary is successfully used as the sleep period time.

Thank you,

Aaron

messages.body_plain:
Hi Aaron,

The documentation for HASPT.algo <https://wadpac.github.io/GGIR/articles/GGIRParameters.html#haspt-algo> does not indicate that "notused" is an optional value. So, I do not understand why you expect this to work. GGIR expects a definition of the time window of being asleep, which we refer to as guider. A guider can be a sleeplog, HDCZA, HorAngle, etc. See documentation here <https://wadpac.github.io/GGIR/articles/chapter9_SleepFundamentalsGuiders.html> for details.

"notused" is internally set when def.noc.sleep is specified as a vector of length two, being the assumed start and end time of the SPT or time in bed. So, this is one option if you do not have a sleeplog. However, in the Cookbook <https://wadpac.github.io/GGIR/articles/Cookbook.html> I indicated that setting HASPT.algo to c() is also an option, if you have no sleeplog. This looks for the least active 5 hours in the day and draws a 12 hour window around it. Whether either of these result into valid estimates of sleep is unknown, but at least those are the options currently implemented. Probably more research is needed to expand and improve the functionality. Funding and/or help for this is welcome.

Thanks,

Vincent

Hello, and thank you so much for the GGIR package.

I am new to using R, but I would like to use this package to process ActiGraph data.
I have used the ActiGraph wGT3X-BT. Some participants have used it on the hip, however most on the non-dominant wrist. I have the raw gt3x-files.
The aim is to investigate sleep in an older population, and also in association with physical activity. MVPA and steps are therefore also of interest. The devices are set to record for a longer period of time than the participants actually wore it, but all were supposed to wear the device for 3 days (24h wear).

Does this code look right, or do anyone with experience have any input on other parameters I should include? And I guess it is best to process the wrist worn and hip worn separately? What is the best way to then process the hip worn?

Another thing is that the devices have collected data at 100Hz. Can I still use GGIR?

#Part1
GGIR(mode = 1:5,
     datadir = "Test_ActiGraph",
     outputdir = "Test_ActiGraph_output",
     f0 = 1,
     windowsizes = c(5, 900, 3600),
     do.enmo = TRUE, do.anglez = TRUE, do.cal = TRUE, spherecrit = 0.3, minloadcrit = 72,
     printsummary = TRUE, print.filename = TRUE, overwrite = FALSE,
     #part2
     data_masking_strategy = 3, ndayswindow = 3, maxdur = 0,
     includedayxrit = 16,
     idlock = 1,
     do.imp = TRUE, epochvalues2csv = TRUE, dayborder = 8,
     mvpathreshold = 60,
     #PART3
     anglethreshold = 5, timethreshold = 5,
     ignorenonwear = TRUE, acc.metric = "ENMO",
     do.part3.pdf = TRUE,
     #part4
     loglocation = "test.csv",
     colid = 1, coln1 = 2,
     do.visual = TRUE, excludefirstlast = FALSE,
     includenightcrit = 16, sleepwindowType = "TimeInBed",
     #part5
     boutcriter.mvpa = 0.8,
     threshold.lig = 45, threshold.mod = 100, threshold.vig = 430,
     part5_agg2_60seconds = TRUE)

Thank you in advance

Best regards,
Mina
